# package iec102

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102"
```

Package iec102 implements the application layer of IEC 60870-5-102, the companion standard for the transmission of integrated totals in electric power systems: its own ASDU model and codec, the time formats "time a" (CP40Time2a) and "time b" (CP56Time2b), and what the controlling and the controlled station share ([State](#type-state), the sentinel errors).

#### Sources {#hdr-Sources}

The text of IEC 60870-5-102:1996 is not held by this project (see docs/STANDARDS.md). Every layout and procedure here is traced to one of these sources, and docs/iec102/INTEROPERABILITY.md classifies each type identification, cause and field by source and confidence:

  - the Beckhoff "Manual TwinCAT PLC IEC 60870-5-101, -102, -103, -104" (TS650x, version 1.3, 2023), vendor documentation of a commercial IEC 102 master, cited as "Beckhoff TS650x manual, section x": the telegram structure (3.2), the type identifications (4.2, 9.1.10), the read commands (4.22.6 to 4.22.29), the integrated totals and single-point layouts (4.25.1 to 4.25.13), the causes of transmission (9.1.11), the record addresses (9.1.8) and the time formats (9.1.12, 9.1.13);
  - recorded traffic of an Actaris SL762B meter (innoWatt icra-tarifes-optic, GPL-3.0, testdata/innowatt) and the test vectors of gisce/iec870ree (AGPL-3.0, used as observed protocol data only);
  - the independent implementations gisce/iec870ree and daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102, read for comparison only.

None of them is the standard. Behaviour supported only by them is an interpretation.

#### ASDU {#hdr-ASDU}

IEC 60870-5-102 does not use the telecontrol ASDU of IEC 60870-5-101 and -104 (package asdu). Its data unit identifier is followed by a record address and the information objects (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 3.2):

	type identification | VSQ | cause | common address (1 or 2 octets) | record address
	information objects ... | [common time tag]

The bodies of this package: [IntegratedTotals](#type-integratedtotals) (M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2, with the optional signature octet), [SinglePoints](#type-singlepoints) (M\_SP\_TA\_2), [ProductSpec](#type-productspec) (P\_MP\_NA\_2), [SystemTime](#type-systemtime) (M\_TI\_TA\_2) and [Read](#type-read) (C\_RD\_NA\_2 .. C\_CI\_NU\_2). Any other type identification, and the end of initialization M\_EI\_NA\_2 whose layout no source gives, decodes as [Raw](#type-raw), which keeps every octet so that the ASDU encodes back exactly as received. A [Profile](#type-profile) interprets the types of a national or vendor profile; the Spanish REE profile is package [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/ree](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/ree) and is never applied unless the caller sets it.

#### Link layer {#hdr-Link_layer}

The serial transport is FT 1.2 (package ft12) with fixed and variable frames and the single character E5h, and the unbalanced procedures of IEC 60870-5-2 (package link) with a link address of 0, 1 or 2 octets (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 3.2). Applications use [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/client](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/client) (the controlling station) and [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/server](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/server) (the integrated total station).

## Constants

```go
const (
	// DefaultLinkAddrSize is the link address size when a station's
	// LinkAddrSize is zero: two octets, as in the Beckhoff example
	// configuration (TS650x manual, section 9.3), the REE profile and the
	// recorded traffic.
	DefaultLinkAddrSize = 2
	// NoLinkAddr as a station's LinkAddrSize selects frames without a link
	// address field (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 3.2: "0, 1 or 2
	// octets"), for point-to-point lines.
	NoLinkAddr = -1
)
```

Link address field sizes.

```go
const (
	SizeTimeA = 5
	SizeTimeB = 7
)
```

Encoded sizes of the time formats in octets.

```go
const (
	RecordDefault           uint8 = 0  // default, if no other value is specified
	RecordAccountingPeriod  uint8 = 1  // counter states from the beginning of the accounting period
	RecordPeriod1           uint8 = 11 // counter states from measurement (integration) period 1
	RecordPeriod2           uint8 = 12 // ... period 2
	RecordPeriod3           uint8 = 13 // ... period 3
	RecordDaily1            uint8 = 21 // daily values from measurement period 1 (22, 23: periods 2, 3)
	RecordMonthly1          uint8 = 31 // monthly values from measurement period 1 (32, 33)
	RecordYearly1           uint8 = 41 // yearly values from measurement period 1 (42, 43)
	RecordOldestSingle      uint8 = 50 // oldest single message
	RecordAllSingle         uint8 = 51 // complete list with single messages
	RecordSinglePart1       uint8 = 52 // partial list 1 with single messages (53..55: lists 2..4)
	RecordPrivateRangeStart uint8 = 128
)
```

Record addresses (list addresses) of Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 9.1.8. 128..255 are for particular applications (private range); the REE profile uses 134..139 for its contracts.

```go
const DefaultCommonAddrSize = 2
```

DefaultCommonAddrSize is the size of the common address of ASDU when [Params](#type-params) leaves it zero: two octets, as in the Beckhoff example configuration (TS650x manual, section 9.3), the REE profile and the recorded traffic.

```go
const MaxSize = 253
```

MaxSize is the largest ASDU this codec encodes or accepts: 255 octets of FT 1.2 length minus the control field and a one-octet link address (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 9.1.6: asduSize 253 for 101/102/103). With a two-octet link address one frame carries 252; the stations split their answers accordingly.

```go
	// ErrTrailing reports octets after the last field of a type this
```

## Types

### type ASDU

```go
type ASDU struct {
	// Type is the type identification. Encode takes it from the Body,
	// except for a [Raw] body.
	Type TypeID
	// VSQ is the variable structure qualifier. Encode writes it as given,
	// except that a [Sequence] body sets the number of objects to its own
	// count. [New] sets it from the body.
	VSQ VSQ
	// Cause is the cause of transmission.
	Cause Cause
	// CommonAddr is the common address of ASDU; the REE profile calls it
	// the measuring point address.
	CommonAddr uint16
	// Record is the record address (Beckhoff: "record address or list
	// address of accounting period", section 9.1.8).
	Record uint8
	// Body holds the information objects.
	Body Body
}
```

ASDU is an application service data unit of IEC 60870-5-102 (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 3.2): the data unit identifier, the record address and the information objects, the [Body](#type-body).

	type identification | VSQ | cause of transmission | common address (1 or 2 octets)
	record address | information objects ... | [common time tag]

### type Cause

```go
type Cause uint8
```

Cause is the cause of transmission octet: the cause 0..63 (bits 0-5), P/N (bit 6, negative confirmation) and T (bit 7, test), Beckhoff TS650x manual, sections 3.2 and 9.1.9.

```go
const (
	CauseSpontaneous       Cause = 3  // spontaneous
	CauseInitialized       Cause = 4  // initialization
	CauseRequest           Cause = 5  // request or requested
	CauseActivation        Cause = 6  // activation
	CauseActivationCon     Cause = 7  // activation confirmation
	CauseDeactivation      Cause = 8  // deactivation
	CauseDeactivationCon   Cause = 9  // deactivation confirmation
	CauseActivationTerm    Cause = 10 // activation termination
	CauseNoRecord          Cause = 13 // requested record (list) not available
	CauseUnknownType       Cause = 14 // requested ASDU type not available / unknown
	CauseUnknownRecordNum  Cause = 15 // record number unknown
	CauseUnknownRecordAddr Cause = 16 // address specification (record address) unknown
	CauseNoObject          Cause = 17 // requested information object not available
	CauseNoPeriod          Cause = 18 // requested integration period not available
)
```

Causes of transmission (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 9.1.11, E\_IEC870\_5\_102COTType). daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102 names 13..18 slightly differently (docs/iec102/INTEROPERABILITY.md); the numbers agree.

```go
const (
	CauseNegative Cause = 0x40 // P/N: negative confirmation
	CauseTest     Cause = 0x80 // T: test
)
```

Bits of the cause octet.

### type IntegratedTotal

```go
type IntegratedTotal struct {
	Addr      uint8   // integrated total address (information object address)
	Value     uint32  // counter reading CR4, CR3 or CR2, unsigned little-endian
	Quality   Quality // quality descriptor
	Signature uint8   // signature octet; encoded only when the body is Signed
}
```

IntegratedTotal is one information object of M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2: the information object address, the counter reading, the quality descriptor and, when the station sends one, the signature octet (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 4.25.2 ff.: "Signature (optional)").

### type IntegratedTotals

```go
type IntegratedTotals struct {
	// T is the type identification, M_IT_TA_2 .. M_IT_TM_2; it fixes the

	Totals []IntegratedTotal
	// Signed reports objects with the optional signature octet. On decode

	// Time is the end of the integration period (time a).
```

IntegratedTotals is the body of M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2: integrated totals of one integration period with the common time tag (time a) at the end of the ASDU (Beckhoff TS650x manual, sections 4.25.2 to 4.25.13).

### type ProductSpec

```go
type ProductSpec struct {
	Standard     uint8
	Manufacturer uint8
	Product      uint32
}
```

ProductSpec is the body of P\_MP\_NA\_2, the manufacturer and product specification of the integrated total DTE: one octet of standard edition, the manufacturer code and a four-octet product code.

The layout is not in the Beckhoff manual; it is the one of gisce/iec870ree (P\_MP\_NA\_2) and its test vector, which read the first octet as month (bits 0-3) and year since 2000 (bits 4-7) of the standard edition. Confidence is low; see docs/iec102/INTEROPERABILITY.md.

### type Quality

```go
type Quality uint8
```

Quality is the quality descriptor octet that follows each counter reading (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 4.25.8): IV (bit 7), CA (bit 6), CY (bit 5) and a sequence number (bits 0-4). The REE profile gives bits 0-4 other meanings (package ree); the octet is kept as received.

```go
const (
	QualityInvalid  Quality = 0x80 // IV: the counter reading is not valid
	QualityAdjusted Quality = 0x40 // CA: the counter was adjusted
	QualityCarry    Quality = 0x20 // CY: carry (counter overflow) in the period
)
```

Bits of the quality descriptor (Beckhoff TS650x manual, sections 4.25.8 and 4.26.32).

```go
type Raw struct{ Data []byte }
```

### type Read

```go
type Read struct {
	T           TypeID
	First, Last uint8 // integrated total addresses, from and to
	From, To    TimeA
}
```

Read is the body of the read commands C\_RD\_NA\_2 .. C\_CI\_NU\_2 (types 100..123, Beckhoff TS650x manual, sections 4.22.6 to 4.22.29). Which fields travel depends on T:

  - C\_RD\_NA\_2, C\_SP\_NA\_2, C\_TI\_NA\_2 and the "oldest integration period" reads (104, 108, 112, 116): nothing (the record address selects);
  - C\_SP\_NB\_2: From and To;
  - the "oldest period and range of addresses" reads (105, 109, 113, 117): First and Last;
  - the "specific past period" reads (106, 110, 114, 118): From, the time of the period;
  - the "specific past period and range of addresses" reads (107, 111, 115, 119): First, Last and From;
  - the time range reads C\_CI\_NR\_2 .. C\_CI\_NU\_2: First, Last, From, To.

#### func (Read) AppendTo


AppendTo appends the fields T carries.

Type returns M\_TI\_TA\_2.

### type TimeA

```go
type TimeA struct {
	Minute uint8 // 0..59 (6 bits)
	Hour   uint8 // 0..23 (5 bits)
	Day    uint8 // day of month 1..31 (5 bits)
	// Weekday is the day of week, 1 (Monday) .. 7 (Sunday), 0 not used
	// (3 bits). The recorded traffic sends 7 for a Sunday and 3 for a
	// Wednesday.
	Weekday uint8
	Month   uint8 // 1..12 (4 bits)
	// Year is the year of the century, 0..99 (7 bits). [TimeA.Time] reads
	// it as 2000..2099, as gisce/iec870ree and daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102 do;
	// the manual names no century.
	Year uint8

	Invalid    bool  // IV: the time is not valid
	TIS        bool  // tariff information switch (minute octet, bit 6)
	SummerTime bool  // SU (hour octet, bit 7)
	ETI        uint8 // energy tariff information 0..3 (month octet, bits 4-5)
	PTI        uint8 // power tariff information 0..3 (month octet, bits 6-7)

	// Res1 holds the two spare bits 5 and 6 of the hour octet and Res2 the
	// spare bit 7 of the year octet, kept so that encoding reproduces the
	// received octets.
	Res1 uint8
	Res2 bool
}
```

TimeA is the five-octet binary time "time a" of IEC 60870-5-102, CP40Time2a: minute, hour, day of month with day of week, month and two-digit year, with the flags IV (invalid), TIS (tariff information switch), SU (summer time), ETI (energy tariff information) and PTI (power tariff information).

Source: Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 9.1.12 (T\_CP40Time2a); the same bit positions are used by gisce/iec870ree (TimeA) and daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102 (CP40Time2a), and the recorded traffic of an Actaris SL762B meter (testdata/innowatt) decodes consistently with them. It is not a time tag of IEC 60870-5-4: TIS, ETI and PTI exist only here.

The fields hold the octets as received, so that a value that does not form a valid date (all zero, for example) survives decoding and encoding unchanged; [TimeA.Time](#func-timea-time) converts to a time.Time.

#### func ParseTimeA

```go
func ParseTimeA(b []byte) (TimeA, error)
```

ParseTimeA decodes the five octets of a TimeA.

#### func TimeAOf

```go
func TimeAOf(t time.Time, loc *time.Location) TimeA
```

TimeAOf returns the TimeA of t in loc (nil means UTC): the wall clock fields, the day of week and SU set when loc observes daylight saving time at t. A time outside 2000..2099 is flagged invalid.

#### func (TimeA) AppendTo

```go
func (t TimeA) AppendTo(b []byte) []byte
```

AppendTo appends the five octets of t.

#### func (TimeA) String

```go
func (t TimeA) String() string
```

String formats the fields, for example "2016-05-01 01:00 SU".

#### func (TimeA) Time

```go
func (t TimeA) Time(loc *time.Location) (time.Time, bool)
```

Time returns the time in loc (nil means UTC). ok is false when the fields do not form a valid date and time; IV is reported separately in Invalid. When the wall clock is ambiguous in loc (the hour repeated at the end of summer time), SU selects the summer or the standard time.

### type TimeB

```go
type TimeB struct {
	Millisecond uint16 // 0..999 (10 bits)
	Second      uint8  // 0..59 (6 bits)
	TimeA
}
```

TimeB is the seven-octet binary time "time b" of IEC 60870-5-102, CP56Time2b: milliseconds and seconds followed by the five octets of a [TimeA](#type-timea).

Source: Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 9.1.13 (T\_CP56Time2b): the first two octets are a little-endian word with the milliseconds 0..999 in bits 0-9 and the seconds 0..59 above them (the manual prints "bits 11..15", which cannot hold 59; the seconds take bits 10-15). gisce/iec870ree (TimeB) and its test vectors agree. daiiniel/IEC60870-5-102 instead writes seconds\*1000+milliseconds as in CP56Time2a of IEC 60870-5-4; that disagreement is recorded in docs/iec102/INTEROPERABILITY.md.

#### func ParseTimeB

```go
func ParseTimeB(b []byte) (TimeB, error)
```

ParseTimeB decodes the seven octets of a TimeB.

#### func TimeBOf

```go
func TimeBOf(t time.Time, loc *time.Location) TimeB
```

TimeBOf returns the TimeB of t in loc (nil means UTC).

#### func (TimeB) AppendTo

```go
func (t TimeB) AppendTo(b []byte) []byte
```

AppendTo appends the seven octets of t.

#### func (TimeB) String

```go
func (t TimeB) String() string
```

String formats the fields, for example "2018-08-18 04:42:25.000".

#### func (TimeB) Time

```go
func (t TimeB) Time(loc *time.Location) (time.Time, bool)
```

Time returns the time in loc (nil means UTC); ok as for [TimeA.Time](#func-timea-time).

### type TypeID

```go
type TypeID uint8
```

TypeID is the type identification, the first octet of the data unit identifier.

```go
const (
	M_SP_TA_2 TypeID = 1  // single-point information with time tag
	M_IT_TA_2 TypeID = 2  // accounting integrated totals, 4 octets each
	M_IT_TB_2 TypeID = 3  // accounting integrated totals, 3 octets each
	M_IT_TC_2 TypeID = 4  // accounting integrated totals, 2 octets each
	M_IT_TD_2 TypeID = 5  // periodical reset accounting integrated totals, 4 octets each
	M_IT_TE_2 TypeID = 6  // periodical reset accounting integrated totals, 3 octets each
	M_IT_TF_2 TypeID = 7  // periodical reset accounting integrated totals, 2 octets each
	M_IT_TG_2 TypeID = 8  // operational integrated totals, 4 octets each
	M_IT_TH_2 TypeID = 9  // operational integrated totals, 3 octets each
	M_IT_TI_2 TypeID = 10 // operational integrated totals, 2 octets each
	M_IT_TK_2 TypeID = 11 // periodical reset operational integrated totals, 4 octets each
	M_IT_TL_2 TypeID = 12 // periodical reset operational integrated totals, 3 octets each
	M_IT_TM_2 TypeID = 13 // periodical reset operational integrated totals, 2 octets each

	M_EI_NA_2 TypeID = 70 // end of initialization
	P_MP_NA_2 TypeID = 71 // manufacturer and product specification of the integrated total DTE
	M_TI_TA_2 TypeID = 72 // current system time of the integrated total DTE

	C_RD_NA_2 TypeID = 100 // read manufacturer and product specification
	C_SP_NA_2 TypeID = 101 // read record of single-point information with time tag
	C_SP_NB_2 TypeID = 102 // read record of single-point information with time tag of a selected time range
	C_TI_NA_2 TypeID = 103 // read current system time of the integrated total DTE
	C_CI_NA_2 TypeID = 104 // read accounting integrated totals of the oldest integration period
	C_CI_NB_2 TypeID = 105 // ... oldest integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NC_2 TypeID = 106 // ... of a specific past integration period
	C_CI_ND_2 TypeID = 107 // ... specific past integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NE_2 TypeID = 108 // read periodical reset accounting integrated totals of the oldest integration period
	C_CI_NF_2 TypeID = 109 // ... oldest integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NG_2 TypeID = 110 // ... of a specific past integration period
	C_CI_NH_2 TypeID = 111 // ... specific past integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NI_2 TypeID = 112 // read operational integrated totals of the oldest integration period
	C_CI_NK_2 TypeID = 113 // ... oldest integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NL_2 TypeID = 114 // ... of a specific past integration period
	C_CI_NM_2 TypeID = 115 // ... specific past integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NN_2 TypeID = 116 // read periodical reset operational integrated totals of the oldest integration period
	C_CI_NO_2 TypeID = 117 // ... oldest integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NP_2 TypeID = 118 // ... of a specific past integration period
	C_CI_NQ_2 TypeID = 119 // ... specific past integration period and a selected range of addresses
	C_CI_NR_2 TypeID = 120 // read accounting integrated totals of a selected time range and range of addresses
	C_CI_NS_2 TypeID = 121 // read periodical reset accounting integrated totals of a selected time range and range of addresses
	C_CI_NT_2 TypeID = 122 // read operational integrated totals of a selected time range and range of addresses
	C_CI_NU_2 TypeID = 123 // read periodical reset operational integrated totals of a selected time range and range of addresses
)
```

Type identifications of the standard range 0..127 (Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 4.2 and 9.1.10, which list them as defined by IEC 60870-5-102:1996). The names are the standard mnemonics.

#### func (TypeID) Family

```go
func (t TypeID) Family() Family
```

Family returns the family of an integrated totals type (2..13) or of a read command (104..123), FamilyNone for other types.

#### func (TypeID) IntegratedTotalsType

```go
func (t TypeID) IntegratedTotalsType() (width int, ok bool)
```

IntegratedTotalsType reports whether t carries integrated totals (M\_IT\_TA\_2 .. M\_IT\_TM\_2) and their counter width in octets (4, 3 or 2).

#### func (TypeID) Private

```go
func (t TypeID) Private() bool
```

Private reports a type identification above the standard range (128..255; Beckhoff TS650x manual, section 4.2 lists 124..127 as "reserved (standard area)").

#### func (TypeID) Selection

```go
func (t TypeID) Selection() Selection
```

Selection returns what a read command of integrated totals (104..123) selects, SelectNone for other types.

#### func (TypeID) Standard

```go
func (t TypeID) Standard() bool
```

Standard reports a type identification of the standard range that the Beckhoff manual (section 4.2) lists as defined: 1..13, 70..72 and 100..123. Types 128..255 are outside the standard range; the Spanish REE profile assigns many of them (package [github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/ree](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/iec102/ree)).

#### func (TypeID) String

```go
func (t TypeID) String() string
```

String returns the mnemonic of a standard type identification, or "TypeID(n)".
